correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the theorem for n>=3 and every real edge weight w with combinatorial Laplacian L(w), actuator b=e0 and positive powers in ordered Kalman columns. Reflection J e_i=e_(n-1-i) decomposes into symmetric dimension p=ceil(n/2) and antisymmetric q=floor(n/2), with constant S and rank-one A_w=A_0+2w f f^T. In pairwise reflected Jacobi bases all offdiagonals are nonzero and w-independent; hence each endpoint-input block Krylov determinant is a fixed nonzero triangular product. A full spectral Vandermonde determinant divided by the two block Vandermondes gives a constant times resultant product over symmetric eigenvalues det(lambda I-A_w), and both polynomial sides extend through collisions. At w=1 the uniform cycle Fourier sine/cosine pairing gives exactly p-1=floor((n-1)/2) common nonzero symmetric eigenvalues, simple in A_1; rank-one slopes are nonzero because a Jacobi endpoint eigenvector cannot vanish in first coordinate. The symmetric zero eigenvalue contributes the affine factor 1+(n-1)w from antisymmetric ramp vector at signed resonance and path nonsingularity. w=0 path Krylov matrix is triangular with diagonal (-1)^j, fixing global sign (-1)^(n+1). Checked parity n even/odd, n=3 minimum, 0 and 1 and negative root, L versus -L convention, and squared Gram determinant. Independently recomputed 112 exact rational n=3..18 comparisons from integer Bareiss arithmetic; finite checks are only corroborative.
residual_risks: Proof requires choosing compatible reflection-sector orientation for an overall determinant sign; evaluating full n=3..18 integer determinants and w=0 path anchor checks this normalization, and the abstract resultant proof supplies a w-independent nonzero constant.
The algebraic finite-Krylov squared volume is not a physical finite-horizon energy Gramian; claim explicitly avoids identifying them.
No formal Lean proof or external expert attestation was asserted.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality survives as the exact signed ordered-endpoint Kalman determinant with its complete all-dimension polynomial factorization and high-order w=1 volume collapse. The 2022/2024/2025 Grudsky–Maximenko–Soto-González line supplies a full spectral analysis of precisely the same graph and is the strongest near-coverage; generic access to eigenvectors plus Vandermonde identities in principle permits reconstructing any Krylov determinant, but reducing their full eigenvalue data to this short closed polynomial entails a nontrivial resultant and normalization calculation that was not identified as an earlier stated or immediately mechanically supplied result. The signed negative root, uniform-cycle noncontrollability, and generic rank tests are previously known and are not independently novel. This is a best-of-knowledge finding with material priority risks and one inaccessible full text, not certification of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: The 2022 same-object complete eigensystem and explicit eigenvector norms could support a shorter spectral derivation of the exact Kalman determinant than currently identified; careful human literature/prior-implication review may affect novelty priority.

The 2025 overweighted-edge chapter DOI:10.1007/978-3-031-80486-1_9 is highly relevant but full text was not obtainable through preprint, OA, or authorized institutional access (disconnected); only publisher abstract read.

The signed singularity -1/(n-1), unweighted-cycle noncontrollability and the general eigenstructure are not new and must never be marketed as such.

checked_sources: Assigned RESULT.md theorem and quantified domain (n>=3, all real w).
Grudsky et al. 2022/2024 spectral same-object literature establishes motivation; known spectrum does not itself display the determinant sensitivity factorization.
Parlangeli–Notarstefano 2011 known cycle controllability obstruction motivates perturbation; Zelazo–Bürger 2014 known signed singular edge gives distinct physical mechanism.
value.rationale: This is a naturally motivated exact invariant of a standard endpoint-actuated undirected ring with a single conductance defect, not an arbitrary slice: the determinant gives an algebraic reachability volume and a complete closed all-n response to changing one edge. The nontrivial dimension-dependent order floor((n-1)/2) quantifies symmetry-restoring controllability fragility that binary PBH controllability tests and signed-Laplacian stability thresholds do not reveal. Distinguishes all w real algebraic roots, physical w>0 controllability, and exact squared Krylov Gram volume. The result is bounded and does not claim a finite-time energy Gramian, other actuator placements or a general graph theorem; its exact, reusable sensitivity law retains value despite antecedent same-object spectral data and a relatively short reflection-based proof.
residual_risks: The invariant is a finite ordered-Krylov algebraic volume, not normalized energy cost; applications to control effort would require additional dynamical estimates.
The result addresses only the endpoint incident to weighted edge, not generic vertices or multiple defect parameters.

limitations: Full 2025 same-object overweighted cycle chapter inaccessible after arXiv/preprint/OA and authorized institutional route; original primary full-text comparison remains a documented scientific priority risk, not an automatic failure.
Prior 2022/2024 published complete same-object eigenvector results could imply the determinant after nontrivial elimination; absolute novelty is not certified.
The algebraic ordered-Krylov Gram determinant is not a normalized finite-horizon control energy Gramian.
Only one input at a distinguished-edge endpoint, cycle n>=3, real w; no claims for other actuators, directed cycles or multi-defect graphs.
